title: Retain counted Partition followed by Balanced
question: Can a bounded per-key count pass avoid two-operation staging through native publication?
summary: Keep the opt-in count-first rewrite. Complete elapsed fell 41%, CLI CPU fell 32%, and managed writes fell from 7.52 GB to 14.7 KB.

workloads: 2 GiB plain UTF-8 input, eight keys, 64 exact parts, 40 MiB cap, one worker, 256 MiB engine setting, 1 GiB cgroup and no swap.

validation.summary: Exact source-row order and membership by key and part, full fields and logical digest, stages, canonical lineage/name ordering, strict physical serialized cap and private cleanup in every timed job; focused source mutation, quotas and empty-root parity controls. Linux default and all-feature workspace tests and lint, WASI compile, native Windows focused contracts, and native default release restoration pass. WASI coverage is compile only for this source revision.

limitations: One synthetic native Linux workload with uncontrolled WSL backing caches.
Finite bound, plain I/O, Auto grouping and unobserved native scope.
Managed traffic omits input bytes, CSV publication writes and physical I/O.
exclusions: Warmup/preflight, initial diagnostic, unused prior builds, and harness attempts that never launched the CLI.
reopen_when: Calibrate selection with wider keys, fanout, skew and platform transfer before proposing default activation.
